headline: Anand Rathi names Marico, GCPL, Asian Paints, and Mrs Bector Food as top FMCG picks

hook: Rising costs threaten FMCG profit margins

headline: FMCG companies face margin squeeze in Q2 due to rising input costs
hook: Input cost inflation pressures Q2 margins
summary: Rising commodity prices, crude oil derivatives, and deficit rainfall are squeezing operating margins for Indian fast-moving consumer goods companies in the September quarter. Brokerage ICICI Direct notes that while revenue growth remains in double digits, EBITDA growth will lag as firms absorb cost inflation. Major players like Dabur, Marico, and Godrej Consumer Products report varied impacts from elevated raw material costs such as palm oil, sugar, and packaging materials. Companies are responding with calibrated price hikes and cost-saving measures ahead of the festive season.
why_it_matters: FMCG stock profits squeeze despite steady sales growth.
winners_losers: Raw material suppliers gain / FMCG margins hurt

Companies are now bracing for potential input-cost volatility in the second half of the fiscal year. Indian retail investors should note that rural demand recovery remains a key variable for FMCG stock performance.
